speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see this newborn has increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin, suggesting jaundice. To determine the severity and cause, how old is the baby in hours, and when was the last time they were fed?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Physiologic Jaundice). The clinical presentation of a 2-week-old exclusively breastfed infant with increasing jaundice and appropriate weight gain (>10% from birth weight) is consistent with suboptimal intake or breast milk jaundice. I will recommend monitoring bilirubin levels to ensure they are within a safe range and to rule out more serious causes like biliary atresia or sepsis.
